arxiv-2104-14338.title: ‘Complementarity’ in paraxial and non-paraxial optical beams Thanks: Corresponding author: pprasanta@iiserkol.ac.in
arxiv-2104-14338.creator: Abhinash Kumar Roy 1 2 , Nitish Kumar Chandra 1 3 , Soumik Mahanti 1 4 , and Prasanta K. Panigrahi 1
arxiv-2104-14338.description: Abstract Establishing the correspondence of two dimensional paraxial and three dimensional non-paraxial optical beams with the qubit and qutrit systems respectively, we derive a complementary relation between Hilbert-Schmidt coherence, generalized predictability and linear entropy. The linear entropy, a measure of mixedness is shown to saturate the complementarity relation for mixed bi-partite states.

arxiv-2207-11470.title: Scale Factor Determination for the GRACE Follow-On Laser Ranging Interferometer including Thermal Coupling
arxiv-2207-11470.creator: Malte Misfeldt *, Vitali Müller, Laura Müller, Henry Wegener, Gerhard Heinzel
arxiv-2207-11470.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Malte Misfeldt *, Vitali Müller, Laura Müller, Henry Wegener, Gerhard Heinzel. The GRACE Follow-On satellites carry the very first inter-spacecraft Laser Ranging Interferometer (LRI) . After more than four years in orbit, the LRI outperforms the sensitivity of the conventional Microwave Instrument (MWI) . However, in the current data processing scheme, the LRI product still needs the MWI data to determine the unknown absolute laser frequency, representing the “ruler” for converting the raw phase measurements into a physical displacement in meters.

arxiv-2305-09061.title: Identifying Disappearance of a White Dwarf Binary with LISA
arxiv-2305-09061.creator: Naoki Seto
arxiv-2305-09061.description: Abstract We discuss the prospect of identifying a white dwarf binary merger by monitoring disappearance of its nearly monochromatic gravitational wave. For a ten-year operation of the laser interferometer space antenna (LISA), the chance probability of observing such an event is roughly estimated to be 20%.

arxiv-2308-11465.title: Computation of covariant lyapunov vectors using data assimilation
arxiv-2308-11465.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by . Computing Lyapunov vectors from partial and noisy observations is a challenging problem. We propose a method using data assimilation to approximate the Lyapunov vectors using the estimate of the underlying trajectory obtained from the filter mean. We then extensively study the sensitivity of these approximate Lyapunov vectors and the corresponding Oseledets’ subspaces to the perturbations in the underlying true trajectory.

arxiv-2406-06864.title: Validating LLM-Generated Programs with Metamorphic Prompt Testing
arxiv-2406-06864.creator: Xiaoyin Wang, Dakai Zhu
arxiv-2406-06864.description: Abstract The latest paradigm shift in software development brings in the innovation and automation afforded by Large Language Models (LLMs), showcased by Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT), which has shown remarkable capacity to generate code autonomously, significantly reducing the manual effort required for various programming tasks.

arxiv-2505-23823.title: RAGPPI : Retrieval-Augmented Generation Benchmark for Protein–Protein Interactions in Drug Discovery
arxiv-2505-23823.creator: Youngseung Jeon, Ziwen Li, Thomas Li, JiaSyuan Chang, Morteza Ziyadi, Xiang ‘Anthony’ Chen
arxiv-2505-23823.description: Abstract Retrieving the biological impacts of protein-protein interactions (PPIs) is essential for target identification (Target ID) in drug development. Given the vast number of proteins involved, this process remains time-consuming and challenging. Large Language Models (LLMs) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) frameworks have supported Target ID; however, no benchmark currently exists for identifying the biological impacts of PPIs.

pmc-11607336.title: De-identification is not enough: a comparison between de-identified and synthetic clinical notes
pmc-11607336.creator: Atiquer Rahman Sarkar, Yao-Shun Chuang, Noman Mohammed, Xiaoqian Jiang
pmc-11607336.description: For sharing privacy-sensitive data, de-identification is commonly regarded as adequate for safeguarding privacy. Synthetic data is also being considered as a privacy-preserving alternative. Recent successes with numerical and tabular data generative models and the breakthroughs in large generative language models raise the question of whether synthetically generated clinical notes could be a viable alternative to real notes for research purposes.

pmc-12504340.title: A comparative case study on the performance of global sensitivity analysis methods on digit classification
pmc-12504340.creator: Zahra Sadeghi, Stan Matwin
pmc-12504340.description: Global sensitivity analysis seeks to detect influential input factors contributing to a black-box model’s specific decisions. This aligns with a key objective of AI explainability: Clarifying and interpreting the behavior of machine learning algorithms by identifying the features that influence their decisions-a significant approach for mitigating the computational burden associated with processing high-dimensional data.

pmc-12639477.description: This cross-sectional study examines artificial intelligence use in health care and other industries according to US firms participating in the 2023 to 2025 Business Trends and Outlook Survey. pmc-12780698.title: Developing and Evaluating Guidelines to Prevent Overdependence on Digital Therapeutics in Children and Adolescents: Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-12780698.creator: Euno Kim, Hajae Jeon, Junghan Lee, Hyangkyeong Oh, Meelim Kim, Jaeyong Shin, Eunjoo Kim
pmc-12780698.description: BackgroundDigital therapeutics (DTx) for children and adolescents with mental health problems have been developed in the health care industry. Despite reports of side effects from DTx for children and adolescents, there have been no guidelines to address the prevention of DTx overdependence among young users.

pmc-12973005.title: Comparative Analysis of Suprapatellar and Infrapatellar Nailing in Tibial Fracture: A Randomized Clinical Study
pmc-12973005.creator: Harshal S. Sakale, Shubham Sakarkar, Alok Chandra Agrawal, Punit Gaurav, Bikram Kesari Kar, Anuj Baghel
pmc-12973005.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Introduction:Tibial fractures are among the most frequently encountered long-bone injuries requiring surgical management. The conventional infrapatellar (IP) approach for intramedullary nailing (IMN) is associated with challenges, such as difficulty in position holding the reduction and post-operative knee pain. The suprapatellar (SP) approach has emerged as an alternative, potentially offering ease in the intraoperative position of the limb, holding the reduction and better functional outcomes with less knee pain.

pmc-13030024.title: Categorization of Jammers for Spaceborne SAR Systems
pmc-13030024.creator: Martin Chiari, Thomas Jagdhuber, Rainer Speck, Madhu Chandra
pmc-13030024.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Jammers can be categorized based on the physical properties of the jamming signal.Three basic categories are jamming by transmission power, jamming by signal shape, and intelligent jamming. What are the implications of the main findings? Jamming effects cannot always be assigned to specific categories solely by their appearance in the resulting image.

pmc-13357105.title: Comparative effectiveness of immune checkpoint inhibitors in squamous vs. non-squamous cervical carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmc-13357105.creator: Li-Fang Lan, Yu-Jie Chen, Dun-Chang Mo, Wen-Yi Li, Fei Yu
pmc-13357105.description: BackgroundThe differential therapeutic efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy in patients with cervical squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) and non-squamous cell carcinoma (non-SCC) remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate and compare the efficacy of ICI therapy in patients with metastatic cervical SCC and non-SCC.

pmc-13527306.creator: Pengting Lee, Benedict C. Jones, Victor K. M. Shiramizu
pmc-13527306.description: Many studies have reported that faces with less distinctive (i.e., more average or prototypical) shapes are perceived to be more attractive. This preference for faces with less distinctive shapes is often explained in terms of a psychological adaptation in which putative health cues are considered attractive.

pmc-13631872.title: A Case of Severe Preeclampsia in the Last Trimester of Pregnancy Complicated by Acute Kidney Injury: A Case Report
pmc-13631872.creator: Vasiliki Koutsia, Emmanouil M Xydias, Zoe Kotoula, Iliana Kotoula, Panagiotis Chouliaras, Konstantina Thymikiotou, Vasileios Migkakis, Georgios Toulios, Apostolos C Ziogas, Ioannis Thanasas
pmc-13631872.description: Pregnancy-related acute kidney injury (AKI) secondary to severe preeclampsia is a rare but life-threatening obstetric complication for both the mother and the fetus-newborn. A 19-year-old primigravida at 36 weeks of gestation was admitted to the hospital with malaise and severe hypertension. Due to severe preeclampsia, delivery was completed by cesarean section.

pmc-13641431.title: Shaping an Early Nephrology Fellowship Curriculum
pmc-13641431.creator: Ashley M. La, Suzanne M. Boyle, Kurtis A. Pivert, Anna L. Zisman, Benjamin S. Ko
pmc-13641431.description: Visual Abstract Introduction Nephrology is an increasingly complex field confronted with an expanding range of therapeutics and rising patient morbidity, requiring both breadth and depth of knowledge. First-year fellows must develop subspecialty expertise while managing a high-intensity workload, often involving greater autonomy, more subspecialized clinical decision making, and increased procedural expectations than in residency.
